proofs.text: Point a repository's `origin/HEAD` at `refs/remotes/origin/trunk` and call `default_branch()`; verify `trunk`. Call it on a repository with no remote made with `init.defaultBranch=master`; verify `master`, not `main`. Call it on a repository whose HEAD is detached; verify `main`

reasons: PROOF-21 happy_path_only: No proof of this rule names a rejection, an error or a boundary.
rule_text: The default branch is the one `origin/HEAD` points at; with no remote it is the branch `HEAD` names, and `main` only when neither can be read, so a repository whose only branch is `master` is never told its approval is not on the branch

tests.body:
def test_the_default_branch_is_what_origin_points_at(project):
    git(project, 'update-ref', 'refs/remotes/origin/trunk',
        git(project, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD').stdout.strip())
    git(project, 'symbolic-ref', 'refs/remotes/origin/HEAD',
        'refs/remotes/origin/trunk')
    assert reader.default_branch(project) == 'trunk'
tests.name: test_a_detached_head_falls_back_to_main
